minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 19, 2013

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Reardon at 5:04 p.m., on August 19, 2013, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 14, 2013, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Leckness
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:06 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Reardon

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Leckness

INVOCATION: Mayor Reardon

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Kelsey Lawrence, M.V.: announced that she wishes to appeal the decision of the Housing
Authority denying her application for an affordable unit at the Ridge condominium complex
because of the value of gifts she received.

City Council Minutes  1  August 19, 2013
 City Attorney Curley informed the Council that there is no appeals process however; the
Housing Authority could ask that this matter be placed on the agenda at a future meeting. The
Housing Authority could either change or reinterpret the regulations or Ms. Lawrence could wait
and reapply for a loan after the appropriate time frame has passed (so that the gift funds would
no longer be considered in the loan application.)

By consensus, the City Council asked for a summary of the gifts that Ms. Lawrence received.

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:09, Mayor Reardon recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received an update in Closed Session but
there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Recognize Capistrano Valley Unified School District Graduate Madeline Hannah for
  13 Years of Perfect Attendance

  Mayor Reardon presented Madeline Hannah with a certificate of commendation.

P2. Presentation on the "Citizens Forum on the Economy" by Independent Economist
  David W. Dickey

  The City Council received the presentation from David Dickey, Independent Economist.

P3. Presentation on SDG&E’s Summer Preparation and Bill Impact

  The City Council received the presentation from Duane Cave, SDG&E External Relations
  Manager.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

29. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  OCFA Division Chief Kirk Wells presented information on drowning prevention.

City Council Minutes  2  August 19, 2013
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Virginia Chavez, San Juan Capistrano: thanked the City of Mission Viejo for its understanding
and support of the arts.

F. Stephen Masek, M.V.: asked the City to investigate power lines near the Stoneridge
neighborhood which are connected to San Onofre. He stated that if the lines are dead, they
should be taken down.

Brian Skalsky, M.V.: discussed a confrontation that occurred between two City Council
candidates during the 2010 election. He stated that Mayor Pro Tem Kelley should not have
emailed her supporters about the incident and he asked her to retract and apologize for the
statements that she made. He also urged the Council to adopt a Resolution barring Council
Members from unilaterally commenting on an ongoing criminal investigation without a Council
vote.

Dennis Lumley, M.V.: announced that the Elks Lodge will hold a bingo marathon on Sunday,
September 1 from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 and from 1:00 to 5:00 p.m. The money raised will benefit
handicapped and disabled children. Mr. Lumley also discussed the Elks' support of wounded
warriors.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed Sheriff's Department’s fees and ways to potentially save
money. He recommended that staff contact the City of Irvine to inquire about contracting with
Irvine for police services and explore other means to reduce overtime costs.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 5, 7, 10, 16, 17, 18, 19, 21, and 23 were removed from the Consent Calendar for
separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

City Council Minutes  3  August 19, 2013
 2.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of July 1, 2013, as
  presented, and (2) approved the Minutes for the special City Council Meeting of July 22,
  2013, as presented.

6.  Check Register Dated July 12, 2013 in the Amount of $1,799,395.89

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  Check Register Dated July 26, 2013 in the Amount of $1,282,906.00

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

9.  Check Register Dated August 2, 2013 in the Amount of $1,086,732.65

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

  Received and filed.

12. Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2013

  Received and filed.

  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for June 2013

  Received and filed.

  Received and filed.

  Received and filed.

20. 2013 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)-Slurry Seal

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Roy Allan Slurry Seal, Inc., in
  the amount of $235,865.00.

City Council Minutes  4  August 19, 2013
 22. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA) Master Funding Agreement

  Approved Amendment 4 to Master Funding Agreement No. C-1-2775 Between Orange
  County Transportation Authority (OCTA) and City of Mission Viejo for M2
  Comprehensive Transportation Funding Programs.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

24. Public Hearing to Consider All Objections to the Proposed Abatement of Weeds on
  Parcels Less than One Acre for the Annual Weed Abatement Program 2013 - Phase 2

  At the hour of 7:17 p.m., Mayor Reardon opened the public hearing.

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  There were no public comments so Mayor Reardon closed the public hearing at the hour of
  7:19 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to instruct the
  Public Services Department to proceed and perform the removal of weeds in accordance
  with Sections 39568 through 39588 of the Government Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

25. General Plan Amendment GPA2007-27, being a City-initiated petition to update the
  Land Use, Circulation, and Conservation / Open Space Elements of the City’s General
  Plan. The primary objectives of the General Plan Update are to: (1) correct outdated
  references in the elements’ narrative; (2) update and correct outdated text, tables and
  maps; (3) review and revise as appropriate the goals and policies of the elements; and
  (4) make editorial revisions. A Program Environmental Impact Report and
  Sustainability Action Plan have been prepared in conjunction with the General Plan
  Update

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Planning Manager Elaine Lister provided background and presented an overview of the
  proposed General Plan updates.

  John Bridges, Principal, AECOM, San Diego: outlined the proposed project and the EIR
  process that staff conducted.

  At the hour of 7:34 p.m., Mayor Reardon opened the public hearing.

City Council Minutes  5  August 19, 2013
   Michele Martinez, Director of the Alliance for Healthy Orange County, Santa Ana:
  congratulated the City Council for the efforts to update the General Plan and for being
  leaders in Orange County. She expressed support for staff's recommendation to include a
  health component in the General Plan.

  Tracy Buyars, M.V.: thanked the City Council for being a Healthy Eating Active Living
  community and for including a health component in the General Plan Amendment.

  Laura Jackson, member of the Sierra Club's Global Warming Committee, M.V.: expressed
  support for the sustainability action plan and for anything that will encourage the use of
  bike and rail travel, as well as solar installations by residents. She further expressed her
  disappointment that the recent electric vehicle charging stations proposal was not approved.

  At the hour of 7:42 p.m., Mayor Reardon closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 13-44 Certifying the Final Program Environmental Impact Report (PEIR) and
  Approving the Sustainability Action Plan; and (2) adopt Resolution 13-45 Approving
  General Plan Amendment GPA2007-27 for a General Plan Update to the Land Use,
  Circulation, and Conservation / Open Space Elements.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Council Member Schlicht announced that she appreciates that staff created a very
  comprehensive report that is required by law however, she voted no on principal. She feels
  that this is social engineering and we are losing control of our government.

26. General Plan Amendment GPA2013-31 and Zone Change ZC2013-20, being City-
  Initiated petitions to establish land use designations and pre-annexation zoning for
  two parcels totaling approximately 3.93 acres of uninhabited territory to be annexed
  into the City of Mission Viejo in conjunction with the development of the Mission
  Viejo Dog Park. One parcel is approximately 2.66 acres and will be annexed from the
  County of Orange. The second parcel is approximately 1.27 acres and will be annexed
  from the City of Rancho Santa Margarita. The parcels to be annexed are generally
  located south of James G. Gilleran Park, easterly of Felipe Road, between Tamarind
  and Fieldcrest. An Addendum to the previously approved Mitigated Negative
  Declaration for the Mission Viejo Dog Park Project (Planned Development Permit
  PDP2011-238) is being processed in conjunction with the proposed annexation of the
  two parcels in accordance with the California Environmental Quality Act

  Mayor Reardon opened the public hearing at 7:52 p.m.

City Council Minutes  6  August 19, 2013
   Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented a brief staff report.

  Planning Manager Elaine Lister provided background on the area that is to be annexed into
  Mission Viejo for the dog park.

  With no public comments, Mayor Reardon closed the Public Hearing at 7:56 p.m.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to (1) approve an
  Addendum to the previously approved Mitigated Negative Declaration for the Mission
  Viejo Dog Park Project (Planned Development Permit PDP2011-238) to include proposed
  annexation of two parcels; (2) adopt Resolution 13-46 Approving General Plan
  Amendment GPA2013-31 for the 3.93-acre Sphere of Influence and Annexation area.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to introduce
  Ordinance 13-298 Adopting Pre-Zoning to Become the Permanent Zoning of Two Parcels
  Totaling Approximately 3.93 Acres to the Annexed into the City of Mission Viejo from the
  County of Orange and the City of Rancho Santa Margarita, California (Zone Change
  ZC2013-20.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

27. Discussion on Use of Artificial Turf (Synthetic Grass) at Single Family Homes

  Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.

  Greg Stones, Associate Planner, provided background on the subject and the proposed
  artificial turf guidelines.

  Laura Jackson, M.V.: expressed support for the proposal to allow artificial turf because of
  the water saving opportunities.

  George Wegner, M.V.: expressed support for the proposal to allow for the installation of
  artificial grass because of the lack of weeds and the water conservation element.

City Council Minutes  7  August 19, 2013
   Motion made by Mayor Reardon, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 13-47 Approving Design Guidelines for Use of Artificial Turf (Synthetic Grass)
  at Single Family Homes; and (2) direct staff to prepare an information brochure that
  incorporates artificial turf (synthetic grass) along with drought tolerant plants and other
  water conservation measures that, including alternatives for other water saving measures,
  for review by the Planning and Transportation Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander responded that there are surveillance

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about the South Coast AQMD Annual Operating Fee

  City Manager Wilberg replied that there is an annual fee for the diesel powered emergency

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to ratify the

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  8  August 19, 2013

*Items 10 and 16 were considered together.

10. City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for May 2013

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she wished to address items 10 and 16 together. She
  asked about cash disbursements in the amount of $493,880.00 out of two different
  accounts.

City Council Minutes  9  August 19, 2013
   Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas noted that this was a result of the DOF
  disallowing the City's loan to the former redevelopment agency in 2010. The City returned
  the monies to the Successor Agency which then sent the money to the County of Orange at

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to receive

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to receive

  NOES:  None

17. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about the Mission Viejo Housing Authority

City Council Minutes  10  August 19, 2013
 18. Beverage Container Recycling Grants

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report and answered questions

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Reardon, to reject the
  proposed resolution.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Reardon and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Ury

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to adopt

19. Environmentally Preferable Purchasing Policy

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to adopt
  Resolution 13-43 Amending Section I - General Information of the Purchasing Policies and
  Procedures Manual, and Establishing an Environmentally Preferable Purchasing Policy.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, and Reardon
  NOES:  Schlicht and Ury

21. Annual Routine Park, Right-of-Way, and Facility Electrical/Lighting Maintenance
  and Electrical Repair.

  Council Member Schlicht asked about $45,000 allotted for additional security lighting at
  the Murray Center along Veterans plaza and stated that she thought the amount budgeted
  was higher.

City Council Minutes  11  August 19, 2013
   Director Dyas responded that staff is breaking the security lighting project into phases and
  the initial expense will be $45,000. Staff will then evaluate the area to decide if further
  security lighting is needed before additional monies are expended.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  award contract for the subject services to C&D Electric, Inc. for the period of September 1,
  2013, to June 30, 2015, in the amount of $489,000; and (2) authorize issuance of a purchase
  order to C&D Electric, Inc. for the period of September 1, 2013, to June 30, 2014, in an
  amount not to exceed $267,000.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

23. Purchase a New Data Domain Backup System

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander presented the staff report and
  answered the Council Member's questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve
  purchase of a new Data Domain backup system for the City of Mission Viejo in the amount
  of $99,308.60.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 9:04 p.m., Mayor Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at
9:20 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

28. Community Services Commission Vacancy

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to appoint
  Cathy Allen to serve on the Community Services Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  12  August 19, 2013
   AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury

29. Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed OCFA firefighter and staff salaries and the issue of
  pension costs and unfunded liabilities.

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

30. Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the Orange County Employees Retirement System

  Foothill/Eastern and San Joaquin Hills TCAs are the top 15 wage-earners.

  Mayor Reardon directed Mr. Wontrobski to the TCA website and stated that she would get
  him additional information if he doesn't find what he is looking for.

  Mayor Reardon presented the Foothill/Eastern TCA report.

31. San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Reardon presented the report.

32. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: presented information from OCERS on its salary and benefit
  study and he discussed pension benefits and the various percentages that agencies and
  employees pay.

  Council Member Ury, responding to the question on pension contributions, noted that at
  OCTA there are several collective bargaining units and each one is different. He stated
  that the OCTA Board recently restructured OCTA benefits so that within 4 years the

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

33. SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented the report.

34. Orange County Vector Control District

  Council Member Leckness presented the report.

City Council Minutes  13  August 19, 2013
 STAFF REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

35. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Leckness

36. Report Issued by Sloan Vazquez Regarding the Analysis of Debris Collection and
  Dumping Rates for Annual Street Sweeping in Mission Viejo

  Council Member Leckness discussed his disappointment in the Sloan Vazquez report on
  street sweeping debris collection and dumping rates.

Council Member Leckness presented a short video on smoke alarms which is currently running
on Mission Viejo Television. He also announced that he has helped to set up a program to
educate South County business owners on exporting their products to China. The event will be
held at the Mission Viejo Country Club on September 27, 2013, and he will provide more
information as it becomes available.

Council Member Schlicht

37. Selection of New Police Chief for Mission Viejo Police Services

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report and the Council discussed the matter. There
  was no action taken.

Council Member Schlicht stated that her agenda report was not against Lt. Wilson but rather her
desire to have a long term Police Chief. She outlined her attendance at recent events including a
GOP Flag Day Salute with key note speaker Senator Ted Cruz and guest speaker Robert J.
O'Neill which provided an inside look at the sacrifices of our service men and women. She also
attended a Congressional Club Luncheon with Congressmen Ed Royce Jr. and Daryl Issa
regarding the work that they are doing to shed light on issues in Washington. She attended a
meeting with the Election Integrity Project regarding election fraud and a meeting of California
United Against Common Core. Council Member Schlicht strongly advised parents to educate
themselves about the Common Core curriculum which is a national education program that she
feels is not good for our children and takes away local control. She further discussed her
attendance at a meeting of SOC 912 regarding Agenda 21, which she noted would result in a one
world government. Council Member Schlicht announced that she had fun this summer cheering
at the annual Brea Lions charity football game and attending a meet and greet function for
Robert Ming who is running for an Orange County Board of Supervisors seat. In a recent poll on
the Orange County Politics blog Robert Ming had the highest number of votes and although she
is not running for Board of Supervisors, she beat Council Member Ury in the poll. She also

City Council Minutes  14  August 19, 2013
 attended the recent Korean War Veterans event, the Pacific Symphony Orchestra, a commercial
broker real estate roundtable, and the Sheriff’s Department's National Night Out. Council
Member Schlicht announced that Governor Brown signed into law the "bathroom act" which she
believes violates the privacy of children. The Pacific Justice Institute has created a Notice of
Reasonable Expectation of Privacy form, designed for parents to fill out and give to school
officials to indicate that they are not relinquishing their child's Constitutional privacy rights at
school (she provided the City Clerk with a copy.) Council Member Schlicht concluded her
comments with a quote from John Adams: "We define a republic to be a government of laws and
not of men."

Council Member Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

38. Multiple Call Party Ordinance

  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley presented her report.

  Lt. Chris Wilson answered questions of the City Council regarding the proposed multiple
  call party ordinance.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, seconded by Council Member Ury, to introduce
  Ordinance No. 13-299 Adding Chapter 11.23 of Title 11 of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code Regarding Multiple Responses to Loud or Disruptive Parties, Gatherings or Events.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Leckness and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley congratulated Chief Wilson on his promotion to Captain. She stated that
we owe him a debt of gratitude for making the City stronger, better and safer. She also
commended the Sheriff's Department for the great National Night Out which has grown from a
small event to one with a very big turnout. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley discussed her attendance at
Mission Viejo's outdoor screening of a new film "The 99ers" featuring footage of Julie Foudy,
Joy Fawcett and the US Women's World Cup Soccer Champions. The movie will air on ESPN
on August 20 and she encouraged the community to tune in and watch it. Mayor Pro Tem Kelly
offered her personal thanks to a young community volunteer, Tina Sahgal, who began helping at
the City while she was in high school in the summer of 2009. Tina came back to volunteer every
summer until she graduated from UCLA and she is now leaving to attend law school in New
York City. She also thanked Public Services Operations Manager Jerry Hill for meeting with the
principal and teachers at Mission Viejo Christian School to help them resolve a weed and debris
problem on a hill near the school. She noted that Jerry's prompt response and service puts such
a good face on the City. Finally, Mayor Pro Tem Kelley announced that the Community of
Character word for the month of August is self-control.

City Council Minutes  15  August 19, 2013
 Mayor Reardon

Mayor Reardon announced that the Employment Development Department is hosting a job fair
for veterans on Thursday, August 22 in the Pacific Ballroom at the Costa Mesa Hilton. She
encouraged vets who are looking for work to attend. She also discussed the Sheriff’s
Department’s upcoming presentation on Drug Trends which will be held on August 29 at the
Murray Center. She noted that two weeks ago she interviewed the County Deputy Coroner and
she was impacted by a story that she heard: The Deputy Coroner, recognizing that a young
person had died of a drug overdose, went to the parent’s home to report the death. The mother
opened the door and she said "I have been waiting for you for seven years." Mayor Reardon said
that she is working on some drug abuse segments for MVTV’s City Talk and she hopes they will
be impactful on the parents and adults of Mission Viejo. She announced that she will be
adjourning the meeting in memory of Community Services Commissioner Joyce
Saltzgiver. Mayor Reardon noted that she and several Council Members attended the celebration
of life for Joyce and it was one of the most moving memorial services that she has been to. It
was remarkable to hear about the kind of woman that Joyce was outside of her work with the
Commission, and she asked for prayers for Joyce’s husband Ron who is very ill.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 11:41 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Reardon adjourned the meeting in memory of Joyce Saltzgiver, to Tuesday,
September 3, 2013, at 5:00 p.m.
